name: High Passes Cantons
inspired_by: The Central Alps where Switzerland, Austria, Italy, Germany and France meet, as of 2026: a glacial lake with a conference town, steep valleys with timber chalet villages, alpine pastures and ski areas, high road passes and rail base tunnels, hydro dams and military caverns. A neutral staging region and arms market rather than a war zone; contracts are security, recovery and evacuation work. In a late-game what-if (game fiction, not a real deployment), covert Russian mountain-troop teams use the high passes and old fortress caverns. srb uses this map as a stand-in for a Balkan mountain transit route. All towns are fictional.
climate: Temperate oceanic in the valleys (Koppen Cfb), subarctic and alpine tundra above 1,800 m (Dfc/ET). Valley summers 20-27 C, winters -5 to 3 C; on the passes winter -10 to -20 C. 1,000-2,500 mm precipitation; snow from November to May above 1,500 m; foehn wind events.
seasons: Winter (Dec-Mar): deep snow, avalanche danger, closed passes, ski crowds
Spring (Apr-Jun): snowmelt, avalanches on steep slopes, passes reopen in late May or June
Summer (Jul-Sep): hikers, cattle on alpine pastures, thunderstorms in the afternoon
Autumn (Oct-Nov): cattle drive down, larch gold, first snow, fog in valleys (inversion)

vegetation: willow and alder on the river
alpine meadows with gentians and alpenrose

terrain.relief: Extreme relief: a glacial lake at 430 m and U-shaped valleys at 500-1,200 m are walled by slopes rising to peaks of 3,000-3,600 m with glaciers; high passes at 2,100-2,500 m connect valleys.
features: road passes with hairpins and galleries
military caverns and bunkers (Reduit-type) in rock faces
terrain.water: A long glacial lake, a valley river with hydro dams and reservoirs, glacial streams, waterfalls; frozen high lakes in winter.

generator.approach: Heightmap at 10 m. Ridged multifractal mountain base with a U-shaped valley carving pass (subtract a smoothed parabolic profile along valley splines), glaciers as a material/ice layer above 2,800 m on north faces, the lake as a flat basin. Hairpin roads generated as switchback splines on slopes.

noise_layers.purpose: glacial valleys and the lake basin

generator.erosion: Hydraulic erosion for gullies and alluvial fans; thermal erosion with a high cap (60 degrees) to keep rock faces; talus cones at cliff feet.
generator.rivers: Valley river spline along the main valley into the lake; dams stamped with reservoirs; tributary streams by flow accumulation with waterfalls at hanging-valley lips.
generator.settlement_flattening: Town on the lake delta flattened; chalet villages on terraces and fans per plot; ski stations on shoulders.
generator.notes: Passes and tunnels are the only links between valleys; avalanche events close roads in winter. Helicopters work only in good weather; AAVs useless except on the lake.

settlements.architecture: Lakeside town: three- to five-storey stone and stucco townhouses with painted shutters and steep tiled roofs, a medieval old town with arcades, a church with a tall spire, grand 19th-century hotels on the lakefront, a modern conference centre of glass and concrete, a railway station.
settlements.wall_class: Stone and brick walls 40-60 cm thick; modern glass facades none; cellars and civil-defence shelters thick.
layout_rules: old town lanes around a square and church
lake promenade with hotels and boat piers
conference centre and station on the edge
every building has a basement shelter

settlements.architecture: Alpine villages: chalets with stone ground floors and timber upper floors, wide overhanging shallow roofs with stones or shingles, balconies with flowers, barns of dark larch on stone piers, a white church with an onion or pointed spire, a hotel, a cable car station.
settlements.wall_class: Stone ground floors thick; timber upper floors thin.
layout_rules: clustered on a fan or terrace above the valley floor
church and inn at the centre
road loops up from the valley

settlements.architecture: Summer alpine huts and dairies (stone and timber), mountain refuges for climbers.

Infrastructure and military: a concrete arch dam with powerhouse, rail base-tunnel portals with control buildings, pass-top hospice, army fortress caverns with camouflaged doors and gun embrasures in rock faces (some now museums or data centres), a border crossing, an arms factory in the valley.
settlements.footprint_m: dam crest 400 m; portal 100x200; cavern door 6x6
settlements.wall_class: Dams, caverns and portals effectively indestructible; control buildings medium.
layout_rules: caverns in cliff faces above roads
factory on the valley floor by the railway

infrastructure.roads: A motorway along the main valley with tunnels and galleries, two high road passes with hairpins (closed in winter), village roads, forestry tracks.
infrastructure.rail: A main line with a base-tunnel portal, a narrow-gauge rack railway up a side valley, cable cars and ski lifts.
infrastructure.power: Hydro dams and powerhouses, pylons over the passes.
infrastructure.airfields: A small military airstrip in the valley (AI aircraft), helipads at the hospital and mountain rescue base.
infrastructure.checkpoints: Border crossings on the passes and motorway (customs, police); security perimeters around the conference centre during events.

pois.contract_use: protect a diplomatic conference or protecting-power mission (clients che, aut)

pois.description: Stone hospice and customs post at a pass with a lake, snow galleries and a border line.
pois.contract_use: secure a mountain pass during a crisis (client che)

pois.description: Rail base-tunnel portal with control centre, emergency station, rail yard and maintenance depot.
pois.contract_use: secure a tunnel during a crisis; counter-sabotage

pois.description: Valley arms factory with a proof range in a gallery, warehouses and a loading dock.

weather.visibility_notes: Valley fog in autumn and winter hides the valley floor while peaks are clear; clouds sit on passes; snow glare; storms ground helicopters.
weather.dust_or_snow: Heavy snow above 1,000 m in winter; no dust (rare Saharan dust tint in spring).

civilians.behaviour: Orderly, prosperous population; commuters and tourists; ski crowds in winter, hikers in summer; farmers on pastures. Police respond quickly; civilians call police on armed people. Shelters in every building.
civilians.casualty_risk_notes: Any shooting near towns or resorts is high-risk; most contracts here should be low-violence.

factions_present.where: Central and western valleys: conference town, passes, tunnel portal, arms factory, fortress caverns (militia army units).
Eastern valley and motorway border crossing; embassy villa district.
Southern pass and border post (Alpini and border police).
South-western pass border post (mountain troops and gendarmerie).
Northern edge border police and mountain troops on exercise.
Arms-shipment escort convoys transiting the motorway (Balkan transit stand-in); consular villa.

Game what-if (proposed, late game): covert mountain-troop reconnaissance and sabotage teams (34th Mountain Brigade-type kit) hiding in high huts, glacier bivouacs and a disused fortress cavern, moving over the passes at night to cache weapons near the base tunnel, the dam and the conference town. Fictional scenario; Russian forces are not deployed in the Alps.

frontline: No front. This is a neutral region: the war sim affects it only through events elsewhere (arms diversion, diplomatic conferences, evacuations of nationals, crises that close passes). Event intensity rises with the global war level and posts security, recovery and convoy contracts. Hostiles here are generic armed criminals (arms traffickers, hired teams) not tied to a faction (proposed) and, as a late-game what-if, covert Russian mountain-troop teams (rus; game fiction). Each surviving rus team raises a valley alert level that posts counter-sabotage, pass-security and cache-recovery contracts; che and aut operations (and player contracts) remove teams, which return only with rising global war level. Avalanche and weather events close passes for both sides.
contract_hooks: Protect a diplomatic conference at the lakefront centre (clients che, aut)
Recover stolen or diverted arms from a fortress cavern (client che)
Interdict a smuggled arms lorry at the motorway customs plaza (client aut)
Escort ICRC / UN / NGO convoys from the logistics hub over a pass (clients che, aut)
Secure a mountain pass or tunnel during a crisis (client che)
Arms-shipment escort along the motorway (client srb)
Evacuate nationals from a consulate villa (clients aut, srb)
Intel grab at a mountain-hut arms meeting (client che)
Hunt a covert mountain-troop team on a high pass or glacier bivouac (clients che, aut; rus what-if, late game)
Counter-sabotage at the base-tunnel portal or the dam against a covert team (client che; rus what-if)
Recover a weapons cache left by a covert team in a fortress cavern (client che)

hot_zones.name: High-pass incursion (late game, fictional what-if)
hot_zones.layout: Covert rus mountain-troop group: HQ in a disused fortress cavern; 3-4 outposts (high hut, glacier bivouac, pass gallery, cache in a barn); Swiss and Austrian checkpoints on the pass roads as friendly anchors; roaming ski and foot patrols; 1 QRF team by night. An arms-trafficker network (generic NPCs) can replace it in earlier phases.

insertion.fob: Staging at a hotel or the valley military airstrip (the player's FOB as a rented facility). Roads, rail and cable cars; helicopters in good weather; no AAVs except on the lake.

early_game_notes: Not an early-game theatre. Generic arms-trafficker NPCs are the everyday threat; rus mountain troops (late tier) are the hostile faction as a fictional what-if added by Captain's decision (2026-10-10). Otherwise a staging region and neutral-contract source at any stage.
